subject: Sampling statements VS log probability increments

messages.author: 6ad5aab4978895bc
messages.subject: Sampling statements VS log probability increments
parts:
Hi Paul,

Firstly, thank you for this package, I have been learning so much about Stan by studying your code. A quick question: in all the models I fit, the Stan code generated by brms tends to express distributions in terms of log probability increments:

target += normal_lpdf(y | mu, sigma);

My natural inclination would be to write the same in sampling notation 

y ~ normal(mu,sigma);

The Stan reference manual suggests that sampling notation should be faster because it removes all constant terms, whereas the explicit notation is more accurate. Is this why you decided to go for log probability increments? For accuracy? Or are there any other reasons?

Thank you,

k.

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Sampling statements VS log probability increments
parts:
With respect to efficiency, there is (almost) no differences, since computing the constants is not the part of the sampling process that takes time.

The reason I chose the _lpdf notation (or better the reason why I switched to it) is because we need the constants to correctly compute marginal likelihoods, which is in turn required to compute bayes factors.

See ?bridge_sampler for more details.
